restrictions: Use only 55-byte messages, drawn as the low 440 bits of two fresh independent uniform 256-bit RAM words. 55 bytes pad to exactly one 64-byte block under FIPS 180-4, so the fixed standard IV is used once and rounds 0 through 30 execute exactly once per message.

The target is executed at most once per sampled message plus two verification calls. Schedule expansion for W[16..30] and all 31 round internals stay inside the single one-unit compression price and are not charged a second time.

Duplicate detection uses a chained hash table on the full 256-bit digest with 2^128 buckets. There is no comparison sort and no full-table scan. Every previously stored digest sharing the query digest's bucket is compared, so a collision present among the samples is always found.

Total time charges all M = 2^128 sampled messages including every failed trial, the head-table clearing, every table store, the expected chain-probe work and the final re-verification. There are no restarts, no rejection loop and no success amplification.

The chain-probe term is an expectation over the algorithm's own fresh message coins with the fixed target held fixed, which is exactly the cost model's probability space. The per-sample fixed cost is bounded, not expected.
memory_log2_bytes bounds peak resident bytes: the head table, digest array, message array, chain links, code and scratch. Memory is a reported metric only and contributes nothing to time_log2.

nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes = 0 is a one-byte upper bound with zero actual advice. Every table is regenerated on every execution; no favorable seed, cached collision, precomputed search or omitted work is supplied.

This is an unconditional analytic construction with no experiment, no computed witness, no hidden precomputed search and no heuristic premise. It does not claim improvement over the nominal reference.
